work: The Upanishads (Īśa, Kena, Kaṭha, Muṇḍaka, Māṇḍūkya)
sourceStatement: Text: the received (vulgate) text as given by Sanskrit Wikisource ({page}), fetched 2026-11-20 and kept in the repository; the few changes made to it (a missing verse number supplied, one verse split across two blocks rejoined, page headings dropped) are listed in source/manifest.json and change no word. {witness} Collation against a pre-1930 printed edition is still to be done. Transliteration: IAST. The reading under each word gives the words with sandhi undone and compound members hyphenated, in the manner of the traditional pada-pāṭha. Pronunciation convention: classical Sanskrit as described in Whitney's Sanskrit Grammar (1889); audio read by Google's Kannada voice from the text converted letter for letter into Kannada script, every written vowel sounded. Translations made fresh from the Sanskrit with Monier-Williams (1899), Apte (1890) and Śaṅkara's commentaries for the traditional sense; no modern translation consulted.
noWitness: No second digital witness of this Upanishad was at hand; the drafter and reviewer check doubtful readings against Śaṅkara's commentary as quoted in it.
notes: One part per section of the text (the Upanishad's own khaṇḍa / vallī / muṇḍaka-khaṇḍa); the Īśā and the Māṇḍūkya are one part each. Units are the source blocks in order, numbered (ln = the section's verse or paragraph number) or not (peace invocations, headings, colophons).
Built on the Bhagavadgītā's machinery (2026-11-20, owner's request: 'Upanishads would be my first choice').
